content.title: New York Knicks vs Indiana Pacers Live Stream: How to Watch NBA
content.text: The Indiana Pacers look to avoid losing 12 straight when they host the New York Knicks on Friday. It’s strange to think that both of these teams were in the Eastern Conference Finals last season. Especially since the Indiana Pacers won that series and are now the first team in the East to lose 50 games. This series against the New York Knicks is tied at one game apiece, but Indiana is now trying to end an 11-game losing streak. The Pacers are just 2-15 in their last 17 games and are in last place in the Eastern Conference standings. It doesn’t help their cause that the Pacers are playing on back-to-back nights against the Knicks, but Indiana is coming off a 137-134 overtime win in Game 2 against the Knicks to even this series on Feb. 10. Indiana ended a four-game losing streak at the time with Pascal Siakam scoring 30 points, while Andrew Nembhard added 24 points with 10 assists. It was enough to hold off a game-high 40 points from Jalen Brunson. Regardless, the Knicks are the big favorite even on the road tonight, with an 11.5-point line in their favor to take the series lead. New York is looking for back-to-back wins against struggling teams tonight, and it is just two games back of the second-place Boston Celtics. New York avoided a three-game losing streak by beating the Utah Jazz on the road on Wednesday, 134-117. Brunson led the Knicks once again with 28 points, and former Jazz member Jordan Clarkson was right behind him with 27. New York was down badly in the second quarter, trailing 49-31, but it rallied by hitting 17 three-pointers and shot 52 percent from the field. OG Anunoby added 22 points, while Karl-Anthony Towns was right behind with 21 to help the Knicks rally. The Pacers may have a better shot if Towns and Josh Hart are out for New York tonight. Both are listed as game-time decisions with knee injuries. The Pacers are coming off a 123-108 loss to the Phoenix Suns on Thursday. Devin Booker went off for a game-high 43 points, while Jalen Green had an impressive game as well with 36. It was the fourth straight win for Phoenix, and it swept the season series 2-0. The 11th straight loss for Indiana gives them the worst record in the league, even behind the Sacramento Kings in the West. It shouldn’t overshadow the good game that Andrew Nembhard had, leading the club with 23 points. At least Indiana doesn’t have to travel for this game on consecutive nights.
